title: Hero hounds
paragraphs: Are you a dog person? Maybe you have one at home and enjoy taking it for walks and curling up with it on the sofa. Personally, I‘m not that kind of person - for me they‘re aggressive, smelly animals that need constant care and lack the independent nature and intelligence that cats have. But given the life-saving skills that some dogs possess, maybe I should give them a second chance.

To some a perfect pooch might be one that looks cute, is loyal and sits when it‘s told but that’s about it - it‘s just a pet. But to really be man’s best friend, they need to do something useful. Some breeds that have amazing sense of smell are put to good use as sniffer dogs or detection dogs, and are trained to use their senses to detect substances such as explosives and illegal drugs. You‘ll often see them at airports or working with police out on the streets.

Other types of working dogs include guide dogs, hearing dogs and mobility dogs all providing a life-saving service to their owners. Some dogs can alert emergency services when their owner has a seizure. And there are clever canines that have been trained to provide affection and comfort to people in hospitals, retirement homes or schools and to people with autism.

New uses for dogs are being discovered all the time. Dr Claire Guest is CEO of Medical Detection Dogs, she says “although the dog has a fluffy coat and a waggy tail, he is in fact a highly sophisticated bio-sensor. You know, evolution has given him this highly sensitive nose, going down to parts per trillion.”

It‘s this incredible ability that has led to the UK’s National Health Service assessing whether dogs can be used to detect early stage prostate cancer - vital for improving survival rates. The dogs - usually from the gundog breed, such as labradors and springer spaniels - are taught to detect a sample of urine from a patient with prostate cancer.

It‘s also managed to train dogs to detect changes in blood glucose levels in people suffering from type 1 diabetes. One patient, who has one of these medical alert assistance dogs, told the BBC that “in the three and a half years we’ve been together, he has alerted and potentially saved my life 3,500 times. And he does it all for a dog biscuit.”

vocabulary.entry: curl up [phr.] /kɜːl ʌp/ 蜷缩；蜷伏
vocabulary.example: The cat curled up on the warm blanket.
vocabulary.translation: 猫在温暖的毯子上蜷缩成一团。

vocabulary.entry: aggressive [adj.] /əˈɡresɪv/ 好斗的；有攻击性的
vocabulary.example: The dog became aggressive when it felt threatened.
vocabulary.translation: 那只狗感到受到威胁时变得好斗。

vocabulary.entry: second chance [n.] /ˌsekənd ˈtʃɑːns/ 第二次机会
vocabulary.example: Everyone deserves a second chance.
vocabulary.translation: 每个人都应该有第二次机会。

vocabulary.example: She takes her pooch for a walk every evening.
vocabulary.translation: 她每天晚上带她的小狗散步。

vocabulary.example: Sniffer dogs are used at airports to detect drugs.
vocabulary.translation: 嗅探犬在机场被用来探测毒品。

vocabulary.example: The smoke detector alerted the family to the fire.
vocabulary.translation: 烟雾探测器向这家人发出了火灾警报。

vocabulary.example: The patient had a seizure and was rushed to hospital.
vocabulary.translation: 病人癫痫发作，被紧急送往医院。

vocabulary.example: Canines are known for their loyalty to humans.
vocabulary.translation: 犬类以对人类的忠诚而闻名。

vocabulary.example: The fluffy kitten was very cute.
vocabulary.translation: 那只毛茸茸的小猫非常可爱。

vocabulary.entry: waggy [adj.] /ˈwæɡi/ （尾巴）摇来摇去的 (非正式)
vocabulary.example: The dog greeted us with a waggy tail.
vocabulary.translation: 那只狗摇着尾巴迎接我们。

vocabulary.entry: sophisticated [adj.] /səˈfɪstɪkeɪtɪd/ 复杂精密的；先进的
vocabulary.example: The laboratory uses sophisticated equipment.
vocabulary.translation: 这个实验室使用先进的设备。

vocabulary.example: Dogs act as natural bio-sensors for detecting diseases.
vocabulary.translation: 狗作为天然生物传感器用于检测疾病。

vocabulary.entry: parts per trillion [phr.] /pɑːts pə ˈtrɪljən/ 万亿分之一 (单位)
vocabulary.example: The device can detect chemicals at parts per trillion levels.
vocabulary.translation: 这个装置可以检测万亿分之一水平的化学物质。

vocabulary.example: The doctor assessed the patient‘s condition.
vocabulary.translation: 医生评估了病人的状况。

vocabulary.entry: prostate cancer [n.] /ˈprɒsteɪt ˈkænsə/ 前列腺癌
vocabulary.example: Early detection of prostate cancer improves survival rates.
vocabulary.translation: 前列腺癌的早期检测提高了存活率。

vocabulary.example: The survival rate for this disease has increased.
vocabulary.translation: 这种疾病的存活率已经提高。

vocabulary.example: Labradors are popular gundogs for hunting.
vocabulary.translation: 拉布拉多犬是受欢迎的猎犬。

vocabulary.example: There are many different breeds of dogs.
vocabulary.translation: 有许多不同品种的狗。

vocabulary.example: The doctor asked for a urine sample.
vocabulary.translation: 医生要求取一份尿液样本。

vocabulary.entry: blood glucose level [n.] /blʌd ˈɡluːkəʊs ˌlevəl/ 血糖水平
vocabulary.example: Diabetics need to monitor their blood glucose levels.
vocabulary.translation: 糖尿病患者需要监测他们的血糖水平。

vocabulary.entry: type 1 diabetes [n.] /taɪp wʌn ˌdaɪəˈbiːtiːz/ 1型糖尿病
vocabulary.example: Type 1 diabetes usually develops in childhood.
vocabulary.translation: 1型糖尿病通常在儿童时期发病。

vocabulary.entry: medical alert [n.] /ˈmedɪkəl əˈlɜːt/ 医疗警报
vocabulary.example: The service dog provides medical alert for its owner.
vocabulary.translation: 这只服务犬为主人提供医疗警报。

vocabulary.example: The dog showed affection by licking its owner‘s hand.
vocabulary.translation: 那只狗通过舔主人的手表达喜爱。

vocabulary.example: The therapy dog brings comfort to hospital patients.
vocabulary.translation: 治疗犬给医院病人带来安慰。

vocabulary.example: Children with autism may benefit from therapy dogs.
vocabulary.translation: 自闭症儿童可能从治疗犬中受益。

sentences.english: Maybe you have one at home and enjoy taking it for walks and curling up with it on the sofa.
sentences.chinese: 也许你家里养了一只狗，并且喜欢带它去散步，还喜欢和它一起在沙发上蜷缩成一团。

sentences.english: Personally, I‘m not that kind of person - for me they‘re aggressive, smelly animals that need constant care and lack the independent nature and intelligence that cats have.
sentences.chinese: 就我个人而言，我不是那样的人——对我来说，它们是有攻击性的、有异味的动物，需要持续的照料，而且缺乏猫所具有的独立个性和智慧。

sentences.english: But given the life-saving skills that some dogs possess, maybe I should give them a second chance.
sentences.chinese: 但是考虑到有些狗所具备的救命技能，也许我应该再给它们一次机会。

sentences.english: To some a perfect pooch might be one that looks cute, is loyal and sits when it‘s told but that’s about it - it‘s just a pet.
sentences.chinese: 对一些人来说，一只完美的小狗可能是那种看起来可爱、忠诚，并且一叫就会坐下的，但也就仅此而已——它只是一只宠物。

sentences.english: But to really be man’s best friend, they need to do something useful.
sentences.chinese: 但要真正成为人类最好的朋友，它们需要做一些有用的事情。

sentences.english: Some breeds that have amazing sense of smell are put to good use as sniffer dogs or detection dogs, and are trained to use their senses to detect substances such as explosives and illegal drugs.
sentences.chinese: 一些嗅觉极其敏锐的犬种被充分利用作为嗅探犬或探测犬，并且经过训练，利用它们的感官来探测爆炸物和非法毒品等物质。

sentences.english: You‘ll often see them at airports or working with police out on the streets.
sentences.chinese: 你经常会在机场或者在街上看到它们和警察一起工作。

sentences.english: Other types of working dogs include guide dogs, hearing dogs and mobility dogs all providing a life-saving service to their owners.
sentences.chinese: 其他类型的工作犬包括导盲犬、助听犬和行动辅助犬，它们都为它们的主人提供救命服务。

sentences.english: Some dogs can alert emergency services when their owner has a seizure.
sentences.chinese: 有些狗在主人癫痫发作时可以向紧急救援部门发出警报。

sentences.english: And there are clever canines that have been trained to provide affection and comfort to people in hospitals, retirement homes or schools and to people with autism.
sentences.chinese: 还有一些聪明的犬类经过训练，能够为医院、养老院、学校里的人以及自闭症患者提供关爱和安慰。

sentences.english: New uses for dogs are being discovered all the time.
sentences.chinese: 狗的新用途一直在被发现。

sentences.english: Dr Claire Guest is CEO of Medical Detection Dogs, she says “although the dog has a fluffy coat and a waggy tail, he is in fact a highly sophisticated bio-sensor.
sentences.chinese: 克莱尔·盖斯特博士是“医疗检测犬”机构的首席执行官，她说：“尽管狗有一身毛茸茸的毛发和一条摇来摇去的尾巴，但它实际上是一种高度复杂精密的生物传感器。

sentences.english: You know, evolution has given him this highly sensitive nose, going down to parts per trillion.”
sentences.chinese: 要知道，进化赋予了它极其灵敏的鼻子，能够嗅出万亿分之一浓度的物质。”

sentences.english: It‘s this incredible ability that has led to the UK’s National Health Service assessing whether dogs can be used to detect early stage prostate cancer - vital for improving survival rates.
sentences.chinese: 正是这种令人难以置信的能力使得英国国家医疗服务体系在评估是否可以利用狗来检测早期前列腺癌——这对于提高存活率至关重要。

sentences.english: The dogs - usually from the gundog breed, such as labradors and springer spaniels - are taught to detect a sample of urine from a patient with prostate cancer.
sentences.chinese: 这些狗——通常来自猎犬品种，比如拉布拉多犬和史宾格犬——被训练来检测前列腺癌患者的尿液样本。

sentences.english: It‘s also managed to train dogs to detect changes in blood glucose levels in people suffering from type 1 diabetes.
sentences.chinese: 人们还成功地训练狗来检测1型糖尿病患者的血糖水平变化。

sentences.english: One patient, who has one of these medical alert assistance dogs, told the BBC that “in the three and a half years we’ve been together, he has alerted and potentially saved my life 3,500 times.
sentences.chinese: 一位拥有这种医疗警报辅助犬的患者告诉英国广播公司：“在我们相处的三年半时间里，它已经发出警报并可能救了我3500次。

sentences.english: And he does it all for a dog biscuit.”
sentences.chinese: 而它做这一切只是为了—块狗饼干。”
